personas.name: Naomi Okonkwo-Pratt
personas.who: 38, K-5 art on a cart. Six 45-minute classes a day, 640 students, no room of her own — the exact physical profile the research documents ('roughly five minutes between classes… physically pushing it down a corridor'). Comfortable with a phone, has no patience for software.
personas.context: MODE 1, the hallway. Tuesday 10:52, iPhone at 414 CSS px in her left hand, right hand on the cart, fluorescent corridor glare, a line of second-graders already forming outside the room she is walking to.
personas.task: Answer the one question the research says is 90% of sessions: who is walking in, what am I doing with them, and where did we leave off.
personas.verdict: Could not answer it. She got a spreadsheet, not an answer — and the app never learns the names of her classes at all, so even a perfect layout could not tell her who is next.
delights: The rotation letter chip is the one thing she can read at arm's length — a big coloured A/B/C beside each day. It is the only glanceable element on the screen.

It genuinely works with the wifi off. Verified: service worker registers and takes control, an offline reload rebuilds the whole week (35 boxes, Fraunces still loaded), and an edit made offline survives a reload. The gym annex has no signal and the app does not care.

frictions.what: There is no now/next anything. The app opens to a whole-week table. Measured at 414x896: 227px of chrome (logo row, tab row, two-row week nav) before the grid even starts, and then 2 of 6 period columns are visible. table.week has min-width:840px inside .grid-scroll{overflow-x:auto} (index.html:1323-1324), so 460px of the week is off to the right.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research names Hallway Mode / Now-Next as the app's headline differentiator: 'an enormous, high-contrast card showing the class walking in right now… One thumb, five seconds, standing next to a cart.' What ships is the opposite — a 840px desktop grid on a 414px phone, read two columns at a time.

frictions.what: Scrolling the grid right to reach Period 5, 6 or Notes takes the Day column with it. Verified: at scrollLeft 460 the .day-name is entirely outside the scroller. No sticky first column, no scroll fade, no arrow.
frictions.whyItMatters: Standing in a corridor she scrolled to Period 6 and could no longer see whether she was looking at Tuesday or Thursday. On a phone the grid is unreadable in exactly the mode the research says is 90% of use.

frictions.what: There is no concept of a class or section anywhere in the app. Columns are 'Period 1'…'Period 6'; the box's accessible name is literally 'Monday Aug 24, period 3'. No grade, no section label, no teacher name, no colour by grade.
frictions.whyItMatters: '3rd - Ms. Alvarez' is the unit of work for this job, and the research builds three of its eight differentiators on it (the what-did-each-class-get matrix, teach-once-vary-per-section, per-section pacing memory). Without it the planner cannot answer 'where did we leave off with THIS class', which is the sentence the whole product is supposed to exist for.

frictions.what: The lunch column is a full grid column on a 414px phone, permanently occupying screen space to say the word 'lunch' vertically at 10.5px (index.html:1348).
frictions.whyItMatters: One of the two visible columns on her screen carries no plan.

personas.name: Beverly 'Bev' Lindqvist
personas.who: 61, elementary general music, 34 years in. Early cataracts plus varifocals; she already runs her browser at 125% and holds a laptop closer than she would like. Not tech-shy — she has kept the same Excel file for eleven years. THIS IS THE COMFORT-PANEL PERSONA.
personas.context: MODE 2, Sunday 20:40, kitchen table, 14-inch laptop, warm lamp behind her, coffee, no time pressure but low tolerance for squinting. Also opens it at 06:15 on her phone in a dark kitchen with the OS in dark mode.
personas.task: Read last week's plans, decide what to reuse, and type this week's.
personas.verdict: She found the comfort panel unprompted, used it correctly, and it made the app worse. In dark mode she gave up entirely — the grid is a white sheet with near-white text.
delights: The settings button is right there in the header beside the app name, it opens a proper modal (736px, focus moves inside), it is a real set of radios with theme / text / density / reading / warm tint / contrast / motion, axe returns zero violations with it open, and the choice persists to localStorage sws.prefs and survives a reload.

frictions.what: Largest text does nothing to the week grid. Verified end to end: clicking Largest sets data-text="xxl" and takes the root font from 16px to 24px, and the tab buttons (39px to 49px), the rotation chips (13px to 19.5px) and the footnote (15px to 22.5px) all grow — while the lesson box stays at 13.5px, the column headers at 11.5px, the day name at 14px, the date at 12px and the lunch label at 10.5px. Every one of those is a hardcoded px value in the app layer (index.html:1325, 1334, 1335, 1344, 1348).
frictions.whyItMatters: The one dial she reached for inflated everything except the words she came to read, and pushed the grid further down the page doing it. She turned it back off. For a low-vision user the comfort panel is currently a net negative on this app's primary surface.

frictions.what: Dark mode makes the plans unreadable. .grid-scroll is background:#fff, a hardcoded literal (index.html:1323), so in dark mode the whole table sits on a white sheet while every string inside inherits --ink #f3e8e4. Measured: lesson text 1.2:1, the week selector #wk-jump 1.2:1, the day date 2.31:1, the 'lunch' label 1.86:1 (on the hardcoded --lunch #EFE6D2), the special-day banner 1.79:1 (on --block #E9E2D2), the tab label 2.29:1. axe: 46 failing nodes.
frictions.whyItMatters: At 06:15 with the phone in dark mode she opened her own planner and could not see a single lesson. This is not a nuance — the app's entire content layer is white-on-white, and the theme control in the comfort panel is what puts her there.

frictions.what: High contrast changes nothing that matters. The rotation letter chip is --ink #2b1d18 on #A8482B at 13px — 2.81:1, 2.82:1 and 2.95:1 for the three letters on screen — and setting Contrast: High leaves all three untouched.
frictions.whyItMatters: The chip is the single most glanceable datum in the app and it is below AA at every setting. It fails because the app-layer rules at index.html:1338-1339 set only a background; the base .chip supplies color:var(--ink) (index.html:645-653), so the intended white ink is simply gone. The in-file comment still claims 'white 12.5px text clears 4.5:1' — the rule that made that true was lost.

frictions.what: axe reports zero violations in light mode, which is how this got shipped. The grid never hits the 4.5:1 rule because the chip text is 600-weight and axe scored it against a background it could resolve, and everything else in light mode passes.
frictions.whyItMatters: A clean axe run on the light theme is the reason nobody noticed 46 dark-mode failures. The build-time contrast enforcement the design system claims does not reach app-layer hex literals.

personas.name: Dre Salinas
personas.who: 29, middle-school PE and health, third year teaching, on a 6-day cycle (Day 1 through Day 6, not A/B). Chose this app over Planbook specifically because the landing copy says the cycle stays correct after breaks.
personas.context: 6:40am, snow day announced, phone in bed, OS in dark mode, then again at 07:30 on the school Chromebook. Emotional state: relief, then a creeping suspicion.
personas.task: Mark today 'No school' and confirm the fitness-testing unit slides forward one cycle day.
personas.verdict: The letters slid. The lessons did not. He now has a year in which every plan is attached to the wrong rotation day, and he only noticed because he happened to read across the row.
delights: Marking a day is genuinely one interaction: gear, 'No school', done. The modal is well built — role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby a real title, focus moves in, Escape closes, focus returns to the gear it came from, 66px buttons, axe clean.

The rotation arithmetic itself is correct. Verified: Mon A, Tue B, Wed C, Thu D, Fri E becomes Mon A, Tue B, Wed —, Thu C, Fri D after marking Wednesday 'No school'. The special day does not consume a letter, exactly as advertised.

frictions.what: Lessons are keyed to the calendar date, not the cycle position. S.cells is keyed 'YYYY-MM-DD|period' (index.html:1699). Verified with distinct markers: before, Thursday held 'LESSON FOR LETTER D'; after Wednesday was cancelled Thursday is rotation letter C and still holds 'LESSON FOR LETTER D'. Friday is letter D holding lesson E. Wednesday shows no letter and still holds lesson C, which is now stranded on a day with no classes.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the app's entire reason to exist, inverted. The research quotes the pain verbatim — 'every time there's a snow day the dates for your next lessons change, which can disrupt your lesson or unit flow' — and calls the fix 'the single most important feature in the app'. The modal's own copy promises it: 'It keeps its boxes but skips the rotation letter, so the cycle stays correct after breaks.' The label is correct and the plan underneath it is not, which is worse than not having the feature, because he trusted it.

frictions.what: No bump, no shift-forward, no undo. There is no action anywhere that moves plans along with the cycle, and SWS.undo is loaded (typeof function, sws-ui.js is in the <head>) and called zero times in the whole app.
frictions.whyItMatters: Once he saw the drift there was nothing to do about it but retype the rest of the year. Planbook advertises auto-bump by name; the research calls its absence 'instantly disqualifying'.

frictions.what: Dark mode, on the phone, at 6:40am: the grid is a white card with 1.2:1 text (see Bev). He read the day letters — which do survive at 4.82:1 in dark — and guessed at the rest.
frictions.whyItMatters: The most common moment to open a planner in the dark is the moment school gets cancelled.

frictions.what: His school runs a 6-day cycle, which fits — but a colleague on an 8-day cycle types 'A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H' and gets back 'A|B|C|D|E|F'. Verified: index.html:1874 slices to 6 with no message.
frictions.whyItMatters: An 8-day or 10-day rotation is common in middle schools, and the app accepts the input, discards two letters, and then generates a whole year on the wrong cycle length. Silent truncation of a structural setting is the worst kind.

personas.name: Marguerite Beaulieu
personas.who: 55, elementary librarian on a 6-day cycle, sees every class in the building once per cycle. The research's 'Mrs. J in the Library' buyer — she currently owns a $6 editable Word doc on legal paper because 'a rotating 6-day cycle is hard to track digitally.'
personas.context: MODE 2. Sunday 19:15, 1280px laptop at the kitchen table, two hands, coffee, radio on. Willing to type. Planning a six-session author-study unit.
personas.task: Write session 1 once and push it onto every Day-3 in the cycle for the next six weeks; write the rest as three-line lessons.
personas.verdict: Both of her two jobs silently corrupted her work, and she did not find out until later.
delights: Speed is real and worth saying so. A fully populated year — 200 teaching days, 1,200 lesson cells, 308KB in localStorage — reloads and paints in 111ms, and ten consecutive week-next clicks take 74ms total. There is no spinner anywhere. This is the direct answer to the research's 'can be slow at times, especially when paging through multiple weeks.'

Setup is one screen and it is honest: first day, last day, days you teach, periods, where lunch falls, rotation letters, your name. Every field has a real <label for>. It generated 40 weeks and dropped her on the right one.
CSV export of the whole year is 201 rows and 291KB in 51ms, with the rotation letter (or the special-day label) in its own column.

frictions.what: 'Fill all A-days' fills the current week only, and fills every period of every matching day. Measured on a fresh 3-letter year: one click from Monday Period 1 wrote to 11 boxes across 2 days — the five other periods of Monday, plus all six periods of Thursday. In a real 6-letter year there are 33 to 34 days per letter across 200 teaching days; this button reaches one of them.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research calls copying one lesson to many 'the defining action of the job' and 'our core verb'. The button's label promises the year and delivers one week, and on the way it overwrites five periods she had already planned on the source day. She lost Monday's afternoon plans to a button she pressed to save time.

frictions.what: 'Fill whole day' from an empty box erases the day. Verified: a Tuesday with all six periods filled, cursor placed in a cleared Period 3, one click on 'Fill whole day' → 0 of 6 cells remain, announced as 'Copied to 5 boxes'. doCopy at index.html:1746 does `if(src) S.cells[k]=src; else delete S.cells[k]`.
frictions.whyItMatters: A destructive bulk delete presented as a copy, reported as a success, with no confirm and no undo. The research asks for exactly the inverse: 'Every destructive bulk action gets one undo toast rather than a confirm dialog.'

frictions.what:
Multi-line lesson text collapses into one run-on string. Typing 'Warm-up: djembes' ⏎ 'Call and response' ⏎ 'Cool down' produces the DOM 'Warm-up: djembes
Call and response
Cool down
', whose textContent — which is what onBoxInput saves at index.html:1697 — is 'Warm-up: djembesCall and responseCool down'. After a reload that is exactly what renders.
frictions.whyItMatters: It looks correct while she types and is wrong the next time she opens it. Every lesson she wrote as steps comes back as a wall. The app's own sample data stores real '\n' characters (index.html:1613) and renders them properly under white-space:pre-wrap, so the feature demonstrably works — it is only user typing that cannot produce it.

frictions.what: There is no undo for anything, and no confirm on the two bulk copies. 'Restore backup' replaces the entire year with no confirm at all — verified: importing a file rewrote 1,200 cells down to 1 with no prompt.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's trust wedge is 'Never destroy on overflow… Data loss in a planner is unforgivable.' Between the two fill buttons and a one-tap restore, three of the app's five bulk actions are irreversible.

frictions.what: 'See a sample first' writes 24 sample cells straight into her real store and there is no way to discard them — no 'this is a sample' banner, no 'clear the sample' button, only 'Erase and start over' buried on the Setup tab.
frictions.whyItMatters: She looked at the sample, liked it, started typing over the top of it, and is now carrying 'Sketchbook covers' in periods she never edited.

personas.name: Tomasz Wierzbicki
personas.who: 44, K-8 art, teaches from a cart two days a week. His assistant principal collects printed plans every Monday morning, and he leaves a printed week in the sub folder — the research's 'admins still ask specials teachers for printed plans… a weekly ritual we can own outright.'
personas.context: Monday 07:20, staff-room laser printer, letter paper, reading glasses, eleven minutes before duty.
personas.task: Print this week for the AP and one copy for the sub folder.
personas.verdict: It printed, it was legible, and it was three pages for one week — the exact complaint the research quotes about the competitor he left.
delights: The print stylesheet is real and it is good. Verified under print media emulation: header, week nav, copy bar, footnote, the gear buttons and the comfort button all hide; @page goes landscape at 9mm; thead repeats as a table-header-group; tr gets break-inside:avoid; and a .print-title appears carrying 'Specials Planner · Week of Aug 24–28, 2026 · Ms. Rivera'. Nothing on the paper says 'tap' or shows navigation chrome.
His name on the printout, pulled from Setup, is the small touch that makes it hand-in-able.

frictions.what: One week does not fit on one page. Printed to Letter landscape with realistic lesson text (about 230 characters per box): 3 pages, with only 2 of 5 days on page one and roughly 130px of dead space at the bottom because break-inside:avoid pushes Wednesday over. At the app's maximum of 10 periods it is 5 pages, with the narrowest cell 44px wide.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research is explicit that this is table stakes — 'a real @media print stylesheet with a one-week-per-page layout, tested and toggleable between compact grid and full detail' — and names the failure mode by quoting PlanbookEdu: plans 'did not print well' and required 'multiple pages for a single day'. There is no compact mode, no 'fit to one page', and no letter/legal choice.

frictions.what: At 11px in a 66px-wide column the lesson text breaks mid-word: 'Sketchboo / k covers', 'kinderga / rten'. .box uses word-wrap:break-word (index.html:1344) and table-layout:fixed gives every period an equal narrow column while Notes gets 150px and Day gets 118px.
frictions.whyItMatters: A sub reads this cold at 8:05am. Broken words in a 66px column is the 'became difficult to read when substantial content was included' complaint, reproduced.

frictions.what: Every rotation letter prints as an identical empty circle. The base print rule at index.html:1219-1224 sets `.chip{background:transparent !important; border:1px solid #999 !important}` for ink saving, which beats the app's unimportant `.chip.l0{background:#A8482B}`.
frictions.whyItMatters: The letter glyph survives, so the information is not lost — but the colour coding the research asks for ('per-class color coding with enough genuinely distinguishable colors') exists only on screen. The base rule was written for the studio's own .chip and this app repurposed the class for something else.

frictions.what: The print button is the only export path he can reach from the week view. CSV and JSON backup live behind the Setup tab, and there is no PDF generator.
frictions.whyItMatters: He wanted a PDF to email the AP and had to print-to-PDF through the OS dialog to get one.

personas.name: Rina Adeyemi-Cole
personas.who: 33, choir and general music, essential tremor in her right hand (mild, worse when rushed). Works from a shared school Chromebook that a second teacher signs into after 2pm, and from her phone. Chose an app with no account precisely because of the FERPA vetting problem the research describes.
personas.context: Between third and fourth period, standing at the shared cart Chromebook in the choir room, 1280px, forty seconds, students filing in.
personas.task: Mark Friday a field trip and add one line to today's Period 4.
personas.verdict: Hit the wrong day's gear twice, then typed her line and walked away three seconds later. The line was never saved, and on a bad day none of the session is.
delights: No account, nothing uploaded, no student names anywhere in the data model — verified, the state is only config, cells, notes and special. This is the trust claim the research says to lead with, and the app actually keeps it.

Keyboard operation of the grid is orderly and untrapped: gear → the day's six period boxes → Notes → the next day's gear, with every box carrying a real accessible name ('Wednesday Aug 26, period 3'), and Ctrl+Enter from a box jumps straight to the copy bar, which then returns focus to the box it came from.
The special-day modal is the best-built thing in the app — 66px buttons, correct focus handling, Escape works, focus returns to the gear.

frictions.what: The gear button — the only way to mark a snow day, the app's headline feature — measures 25x27px and is floated into the top-right corner of the day cell (index.html:1340: float:right; font-size:14px; padding:2px 4px). It does not grow at Largest text: still 27px at data-text="xxl".
frictions.whyItMatters: Against a --tap floor of 44px this is a third of the area, five of them stacked 100px apart vertically, and the thing directly beneath each one is a contenteditable box. A missed tap puts a cursor into a lesson she did not mean to edit. The design system calls 44px a hard invariant, not a preference.

frictions.what: An edit is lost if the page goes away within 400ms. Verified with a box holding a known prior value: type, wait 50ms, reload → the old value is back. queueSave debounces 400ms (index.html:1502) and there is no pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload flush anywhere in the file — dispatching pagehide after a 50ms edit leaves the change unwritten.
frictions.whyItMatters: Her whole interaction pattern is type-one-line-and-walk-away, on a machine another teacher is about to claim. On a phone the screen locking mid-sentence does the same thing. Seating Chart already ships the pagehide flush this app lacks.

frictions.what: When a write fails, the header says 'Saved' anyway. With setItem throwing QuotaExceededError, the 'Saved' pill still fades in (opacity 0.99), localStorage holds nothing, no warning appears anywhere, and the next reload drops her at the 'Plan your whole year once' welcome screen with the year gone. store.set at index.html:1463 swallows the exception into an in-memory object that store.get can never read back, because get returns localStorage's null first.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research names this as the single best trust wedge available — 'Never destroy on overflow. Local-first storage with an explicit versioned autosave, a visible last saved indicator'. What ships is a green 'Saved' that is not evidence of anything. On a managed school Chromebook with storage restrictions this is a whole year, silently.

frictions.what: The copy bar slides up over the bottom of the page every time any period box takes focus. Measured at 414x720: the bar is 101px tall with its top edge at y=619, covering 2 of the 5 day rows.
frictions.whyItMatters: The design system's hard invariant reads 'Nothing appears over a primary surface… Nothing in the thumb zone moves, grows, or animates.' This is an animated 101px panel that arrives unbidden in the thumb zone on every focus, over the rows she is trying to read, carrying two destructive buttons.

frictions.what: The 'Saved' indicator is aria-hidden="true" (index.html:1421) and nothing else announces a save, while the live region announces week changes and copy counts.
frictions.whyItMatters: The one status a screen-reader user most needs from a local-first app — did it save — is the one deliberately hidden from them.

worksWell: Offline is real, not a claim. The service worker registers, takes control, and an offline reload rebuilds the entire week — 35 boxes, self-hosted Fraunces still loaded, zero console errors — and an edit made offline persists across a reload. For a PE teacher on a field and a music teacher in a basement annex, this alone beats iDoceo (Apple-only) and PlanbookEdu (internet required) at once.

Speed at real scale. A full year of 200 teaching days and 1,200 lesson cells (308KB) reloads and paints in 111ms; ten consecutive week jumps cost 74ms total; CSV of the whole year is 201 rows in 51ms. No spinner exists anywhere in the app.
The rotation arithmetic is correct. Marking a day special does not consume a letter, so the cycle itself stays true across breaks — verified letter-by-letter across a cancelled Wednesday.
Text safety is airtight. '">

The special-day modal is the best-built component in the portfolio's app layer: role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby a real title, focus moved in, a working Tab trap, Escape, focus returned to the originating gear, 66px buttons, axe clean.
Keyboard operation of the grid is orderly and untrapped, every contenteditable box carries a real accessible name, Ctrl+Enter reaches the copy bar, and focus returns to the source box after a copy.

Setup is one honest screen with real <label for> on every field, and it survives numeric abuse: 0, '', 'abc' → 6 periods; -3 → 1; 99 and 1e9 → 10. No NaN, Infinity, undefined or [object anywhere on screen under any input tested.

Bad input files are handled: a non-backup JSON produces 'That file doesn't look like a Specials Planner backup' and leaves the existing year untouched; a corrupt localStorage value boots cleanly to the welcome screen with no uncaught error.
No account, no upload, no student names in the data model at all — the FERPA position the research says to lead with is actually kept.
hurts: Lessons are keyed to calendar dates, not cycle positions. After one snow day the letters shift and the plans do not: Thursday becomes letter C and still holds lesson D. The app's headline promise is printed in the modal and contradicted by the data model underneath it.

Dark mode makes the content invisible. .grid-scroll{background:#fff} is a hardcoded literal, so lesson text renders at 1.2:1 and the week selector at 1.2:1. 46 failing nodes under axe, zero in light mode.

The comfort panel cannot reach the grid. Largest text takes the root from 16px to 24px and the lesson box stays at 13.5px, the column headers at 11.5px, the date at 12px and the lunch label at 10.5px, all hardcoded px. High contrast does not touch the 2.81:1 rotation chip.
Multi-line lesson text collapses to a run-on string the next time the app opens, because textContent is read off a contenteditable div that stores line breaks as child <div>s.

The two bulk-copy buttons are destructive and irreversible. 'Fill all A-days' reaches 1 of 33 A-days in a real year and overwrites five other periods on the source day; 'Fill whole day' from an empty box deletes the day and reports 'Copied to 5 boxes'. SWS.undo is loaded and called zero times.

Nothing guarantees a save. A 400ms debounce with no pagehide flush loses the last edit to a reload or a screen lock, and a failed write shows the green 'Saved' pill anyway and drops the whole year on the next load.
There are no classes. Periods are numbers, so the app cannot answer 'who is walking in and where did we leave off with them' — the question the research says 90% of sessions exist to ask.
On a phone the product is an 840px desktop table read two columns at a time, with 227px of chrome above it and a Day column that scrolls away.
Print is three pages for one week with mid-word breaks in 66px columns, and five pages at 10 periods.
Structural settings truncate silently: 7+ rotation letters slice to 6, a multi-year span stops at 80 weeks (Aug 2026 → May 2028 builds through 3 Mar 2028 and says nothing).

'No weeks yet — check your year dates in Setup' is shown when the dates are fine and workDays is the problem, which is the research's 'error telling me to pick a valid start time, but nothing is wrong with the time I pick' complaint, reproduced.
mostWantedNext: Key lessons to cycle position, not to the date — plan[letter][period] with the calendar as a rendered projection — and add the one-tap bump with an undo toast. This is the app's reason to exist and everything else in the category is downstream of it.

A class/section layer: name the class in each period slot ('3rd — Alvarez'), colour by grade, and let a lesson be authored once and assigned to every section of a grade, with a per-section 'where we left off' line.
A Now/Next hallway card as the phone default: the class walking in, the lesson, the materials line, one thumb, nothing else on screen.
Undo on every destructive action, using the SWS.undo runtime that is already loaded — the two fill buttons, restore-from-backup, and erase.
Fix the grid's typography and colour so the comfort panel reaches it: tokens instead of the eight hardcoded px sizes and the #fff / #EFE6D2 / #E9E2D2 literals.
A one-week-on-one-page print mode with a compact/full toggle and letter/legal choice, plus a direct PDF button from the week view.
A save you can trust: pagehide flush, a visible timestamped 'saved 12:41' rather than a fading pill, and a loud, actionable warning the moment a write fails.
Sticky Day column, a scroll affordance on the grid, and a 44px snow-day control.

scenarios.name: The standard battery (node design/stress.mjs specials-planner)
scenarios.method: Ran the shipped battery unmodified and read every line of its output against what the app actually contains.
scenarios.result: 0 hard failures. Layout clean at 320/414/1280 and at largest-text and roomy; touch targets under 32px = []; hostile text clean; numeric edges clean; 30 rapid clicks in 448ms; reload persistence 1432→1432 chars; corrupt storage boots; keyboard reachability 7 focusable, 0 unreachable; axe clean; no console errors. BUT: 'bulk: 200 rapid adds' reports {"ran":false} and 'keyboard reachability' finds only 7 focusable elements — the battery never left the welcome screen, because entering the app requires clicking 'Start fresh' or 'See a sample first' and there are no text inputs on that screen for it to grab.
scenarios.defect: Not an app defect — a coverage gap. Every 'clean' line above describes a marketing page with three buttons on it. All 46 dark-mode contrast failures, the 25px gear, the 840px grid, the frozen type scale and every data-loss path below sit behind that one click.

scenarios.name: The week grid at phone, tablet and desktop widths
scenarios.method: Loaded the sample year and measured .grid-scroll and table.week at 320, 414 and 1280 CSS px, plus the computed position of the first body cell.
scenarios.result: table.week is min-width:840px at every width. At 320px: 554px hidden. At 414px: 460px hidden. At 1280px (inside --wrap 66rem): 202px hidden. The Day column is position:static, so scrolling to the Notes column (scrollLeft 460 at 414px) puts .day-name entirely outside the scroller. Document-level overflow is 0 at every size — the page itself never scrolls sideways, which is correct. 227px of chrome sits above the grid at 414x896, leaving 2 of 6 period columns visible.
scenarios.defect: The primary surface is a fixed 840px desktop table with no sticky first column and no scroll affordance. On the device the research says carries 90% of sessions, the week is read two columns at a time and loses its row labels when you scroll.

scenarios.name: Dark mode across the whole app
scenarios.method: Ran the app at colorScheme:'dark', read computed colours off every grid element, ran axe restricted to color-contrast, and captured a full-page screenshot.
scenarios.result: .grid-scroll background resolves to rgb(255,255,255) — a hardcoded #fff at index.html:1323. Lesson text #f3e8e4 on that white = 1.2:1. #wk-jump (background:#fff at :1318) = 1.2:1. .day-date = 2.31:1. td.lunch span on --lunch #EFE6D2 = 1.86:1. .sp-banner on --block #E9E2D2 = 1.79:1. .tab = 2.29:1. #modal input background #fff with #f3e8e4 text — you cannot see what you type into the custom day label. .saved is a hardcoded #55704F. axe color-contrast: 46 failing nodes in dark, 0 in light.

scenarios.name: Comfort panel driven for real, then measured on the grid
scenarios.method: Clicked #swsPrefsBtn, clicked the Largest and High-contrast radios inside #swsPrefs the way a user would, closed with Escape, then read computed font sizes and target heights off the week grid. Repeated as harness prefs at text:xxl, contrast:more, density:roomy and 320px.
scenarios.result: The panel itself is faultless: opens 736px tall, focus inside, axe 0 violations, writes data-text="xxl" and data-contrast="more", root font 16px → 24px, persists to sws.prefs. What it reaches: .tab 39px → 49px, .chip 13px → 19.5px, .footnote 15px → 22.5px. What it does not reach: .box 13.5px (unchanged), th 11.5px (unchanged), .day-name 14px (unchanged), .day-date 12px (unchanged), td.lunch span 10.5px (unchanged), .day-gear 27px (unchanged), table.week min-width 840px (unchanged), hidden grid width 460px (unchanged). High contrast leaves the 2.81:1 rotation chip at 2.81:1.

scenarios.name: Rotation-letter chip contrast
scenarios.method: Computed WCAG contrast for the rendered .chip.l0/.l1/.l2 in light and dark, at default and at contrast:more, and cross-checked why axe stays silent.
scenarios.result: Light: #2b1d18 on #A8482B = 2.81:1, on #3E6E6B = 2.82:1, on #55704F = 2.95:1, at 13px/600. contrast:more: unchanged. Dark: #f3e8e4 on the same fills = 4.82:1 (passes). The in-file comment above line 1338 still asserts 'white 12.5px text clears 4.5:1 (WCAG AA)' — the rule that set that colour no longer exists in the file.

scenarios.name: Snow day: does the plan move with the cycle?
scenarios.method: Built a 6-letter year, wrote distinct markers ('LESSON FOR LETTER A'…'E') into Period 1 of each of week one's five days, then marked Wednesday 'No school' through the real gear/modal path and re-read every row.
scenarios.result: Letters before: Mon A, Tue B, Wed C, Thu D, Fri E. Letters after: Mon A, Tue B, Wed (none, banner 'No school'), Thu C, Fri D — the rotation itself is correct. Content after: Thu shows letter C holding 'LESSON FOR LETTER D'; Fri shows letter D holding 'LESSON FOR LETTER E'; Wed holds 'LESSON FOR LETTER C' on a day with no classes. S.cells is keyed 'YYYY-MM-DD|period' (index.html:1699). No bump action exists; SWS.undo is loaded and never called.
scenarios.defect: The app renders the cycle correctly and stores the lessons against dates, so one cancellation permanently desynchronises every plan from its rotation day for the rest of the year — the exact failure the product exists to solve, with the fix promised in the modal's own copy.

scenarios.name: Multi-line lesson text through the contenteditable boxes

Call and response
Cool down
'. textContent, which is what onBoxInput persists (index.html:1697): 'Warm-up: djembesCall and responseCool down'. Stored value identical. After reload the box renders that run-on string. Paste is handled correctly (plainPaste strips formatting via insertText) and the app's own sample data stores real \n characters, which render fine under white-space:pre-wrap — so the storage format supports line breaks and only typed input cannot produce them.

scenarios.name: The two bulk-copy buttons
scenarios.method: On a fresh 3-letter year, typed a marker into Monday Period 1, clicked 'Fill all A-days', and counted the cells that received it and the days they fell on. Separately filled all six periods of a Tuesday, cleared Period 3, and clicked 'Fill whole day' from the now-empty box. Also computed how many days share a letter in a real 6-letter year.

Scope is `const w=YEAR[curWeek]` (index.html:1731), the current week only. A real 6-letter, 200-teaching-day year has 33–34 days per letter. 'Fill whole day' from an empty box: Tuesday went from 6 filled cells to 0, announced 'Copied to 5 boxes'. No confirm, no undo, zero undo controls in the DOM.
scenarios.defect: The app's core verb is week-scoped while its label promises the year; it overwrites periods the user did not select; and used from an empty cell it is a silent bulk delete reported as a copy.

scenarios.name: Does a save actually happen?
scenarios.method: With a box holding a known prior value, typed a change, waited 50ms, and reloaded. Repeated at 600ms. Dispatched pagehide 50ms after an edit and inspected localStorage. Then patched Storage.prototype.setItem to throw QuotaExceededError for the app's key and used the app normally.
scenarios.result: 50ms → the old value is back; the edit is gone. 600ms → the edit survives (queueSave debounces 400ms, index.html:1502). pagehide after 50ms → the pending edit is NOT written; there is no pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload handler anywhere in the file. With setItem throwing: the 'Saved' pill still animates to opacity 0.99, localStorage.getItem('palette2') is null, no warning text appears anywhere on the page, and the next reload lands on the welcome screen with the year gone. store.set (index.html:1463) catches and writes to an in-memory object that store.get (index.html:1462) can never return, because it returns localStorage's null first.
scenarios.defect: Two independent data-loss paths: the last 400ms of typing dies with the tab, and a failed write is reported to the user as a successful one.

scenarios.name: A full school year at scale
scenarios.method: Seeded every period of every teaching day of a default year with ~230 characters of realistic lesson text plus a daily note, then reloaded and paged.
scenarios.result: 200 teaching days, 1,200 lesson cells, 308,597 bytes in localStorage. Reload to painted grid: 111ms. Ten consecutive 'next week' clicks: 74ms total. Page overflow 0. Zero console errors. The 40-option week <select> renders instantly.

scenarios.name: Print to PDF and read the paper
scenarios.method: Filled a week with realistic lesson text, emulated print media, measured what survives, then generated Letter-landscape PDFs at 6 and at 10 periods and rendered the pages to images to look at them.
scenarios.result: Chrome correctly hidden: header, .weeknav, #bar, .footnote, .day-gear, #swsPrefsBtn all display:none; .print-title appears reading 'Specials Planner · Week of Aug 24–28, 2026 · Ms. Rivera'; @page landscape 9mm; thead repeats; tr break-inside:avoid. But the table is 1,044px tall against ~748px of usable page: 3 pages for one 6-period week, with only Monday and Tuesday on page one and ~130px of dead space at its foot. At 10 periods: 13 columns, 1,909px tall, 5 pages, narrowest cell 44px. Lesson text sets at 11px in ~66px columns and breaks mid-word ('Sketchboo / k covers'). Every rotation chip prints as an identical empty circle because the base print rule `.chip{background:transparent !important}` (index.html:1219-1224) outranks `.chip.l0{background:#A8482B}`.
scenarios.defect: One week is three pages and the colour coding does not survive to paper. The research names one-week-per-page as table stakes and quotes 'plans did not print well… requiring multiple pages for a single day' as the competitor complaint to beat.

scenarios.name: CSV export: correctness, encoding, and formulas
scenarios.method: Exported the full seeded year, then re-exported with a cell containing '=HYPERLINK("http://evil.test","claim your prize")' and one containing 'Señor Nguyễn · 音楽 · résumé'.
scenarios.result: specials-planner-2026.csv, 201 rows, 291,721 bytes, 51ms. Header 'Date,Weekday,Rotation,Period 1…Period 6,Notes'. Quoting is correct — embedded quotes doubled, commas and newlines wrapped. Special days put their label in the Rotation column. Unicode is written correctly as UTF-8 but the blob has NO BOM (charCodeAt(0) = 68, 'D'), so Excel on Windows will mojibake accented and CJK text. The formula cell is exported verbatim as a live formula.
scenarios.defect: Two small ones on a path the research treats as a differentiator (the Sheets/Excel escape hatch): no UTF-8 BOM, so non-ASCII lesson text corrupts in Excel; and no formula-injection guard, so a lesson line pasted from a website that begins with =, +, - or @ becomes an executable formula in the teacher's spreadsheet.

scenarios.name: Corrupt, legacy and hostile saved state
scenarios.method: Wrote six malformed states into the palette2 key and reloaded each, plus outright garbage, plus a non-backup file through the real 'Restore backup' file picker.
scenarios.result: lunchAfter:'noon' → the lunch column disappears entirely (0 lunch headers, 8 columns instead of 9), no error, no message; caused by `+c.lunchAfter??2` at index.html:1493, where unary plus binds tighter than ?? so NaN survives. periods:'six' → recovers to 6. cells:[] survives migrate() untouched (`s.cells=s.cells||{}`) and then serialises back through JSON.stringify as `"cells":[]` with every lesson discarded. workDays:['Mon'] → 'No weeks yet — Check your year dates in Setup', which is the wrong diagnosis. end-before-start and junk dates → the same generic message. Garbage JSON → clean boot to the welcome screen, no uncaught error, but also no 'your file looked damaged' and no way to see or recover the raw text. A non-backup JSON through the file picker → 'That file doesn't look like a Specials Planner backup' and the existing year is untouched (24 cells intact). No uncaught exceptions in any case.
scenarios.defect: No crashes — but three silent wrong states: a lost lunch column from an operator-precedence bug, total lesson loss if cells is ever an array, and an unactionable error message that blames the dates when the teaching days are the problem.

scenarios.name: Hostile text and injection
scenarios.method: Filled the custom day-label field with '">' and saved; put 'B' and 300 'A's into the rotation-letters field; typed script payloads into lesson boxes.
scenarios.result: window.__pwned and __pwned2 both false; zero img[src=x] nodes; the banner renders the payload as literal text; zero <b> elements inside any chip. esc() (index.html:1556) escapes & < > " and every attribute in the template is double-quoted; lesson text reaches the DOM only via textContent. The 300-character rotation letter is accepted whole and renders a 4,063px-wide chip inside a 118px Day cell (page overflow still 0 — .grid-scroll clips it).
scenarios.defect: No injection of any kind. The only issue is cosmetic: there is no length cap on a rotation letter, so one long string destroys the Day column.

scenarios.name: Numeric and structural edges in Setup
scenarios.method: Applied '0', '-3', '99', '2.7', '1e9', '' and 'abc' to Periods per day; gave nine rotation letters; set a two-year span; then scanned the whole page for NaN/Infinity/undefined/[object.
scenarios.result: 0 → 6, '' → 6, 'abc' → 6 (falsy-or-default at index.html:1872), -3 → 1, 99 → 10, 1e9 → 10, 2.7 → stored as 2.7 and rendered as 2 period columns. No NaN, Infinity, undefined or [object anywhere. Nine letters 'A…I' → stored as A|B|C|D|E|F, silently sliced to 6 (index.html:1874). A 2026-08-24 → 2028-05-26 span builds 80 weeks ending 'Wk 80 · Feb 28 – Mar 3, 2028' while config.yearEnd still reads 2028-05-26 — the `guard++<80` cap at index.html:1532 — with no warning anywhere.
scenarios.defect: Three silent structural truncations: a typed 0/blank/garbage becomes 6 rather than being rejected, an 8- or 10-day cycle is cut to 6 letters, and any span past 80 weeks stops early. Each of these makes a whole generated year quietly wrong.

scenarios.name: Touch targets and the thumb zone
scenarios.method: Ran smallTargets() on the week view and the setup view at 414px, measured the copy bar's geometry at 414x720, and re-measured everything at data-text="xxl".
scenarios.result: Week view: .day-gear 25x27px (five of them), .tab 38px, #swsPrefsBtn 36px. Setup view: seven .dp day buttons at 44x38px. At Largest text .tab grows to 49px but .day-gear stays 27px. The copy bar (#bar, index.html:1353) is position:fixed bottom:0 with a transform transition, 101px tall, top edge at y=619 in a 720px viewport — covering 2 of the 5 day rows — and it slides in on focus of any period box, unbidden.
scenarios.defect: The snow-day control is a third of the 44px floor and does not scale; and an animated 101px panel enters the thumb zone over the primary surface on every focus, which the design system lists as a hard invariant against ('Nothing appears over a primary surface… Nothing in the thumb zone moves, grows, or animates').

scenarios.name: Keyboard walk and the copy-bar path
scenarios.method: Tabbed 24 stops through the week view logging activeElement, counted the focusable set, then drove the copy bar entirely from the keyboard and checked where focus landed afterwards.
scenarios.result: Order is orderly and untrapped: wk-next → wk-jump → wk-today → wk-print → gear → the day's six period boxes → Notes → next day's gear. 35 contenteditable boxes per week, 51 focusable-ish nodes; reaching Friday's Notes costs about 33 Tab presses and there is no arrow-key grid navigation. Ctrl+Enter from a box moves focus to #bar-day as advertised, Enter fires the copy, and focus returns to the source box. #bar-hint is aria-live=polite and #live carries 'Copied to 5 boxes'. Escape hides the bar.
scenarios.defect: No blocker — the keyboard path works, which is more than most of the portfolio. The cost is navigational: 33 stops to cross one week, with no arrow keys and no way to jump between periods.

scenarios.name: Offline, for real
scenarios.method: Served the app on localhost so the registration guard applies, loaded it, confirmed the service worker took control, then set the context offline and reloaded, edited and reloaded again.
scenarios.result: Registered, active and controlling. Offline reload rebuilds the full week — table present, 35 boxes, Fraunces reporting status 'loaded', title intact, zero page or console errors. An edit typed while offline survives a subsequent offline reload. The SHELL list in sw.js covers index.html, privacy.html, the manifest, all three icons, both self-hosted woff2 files, sws-prefs.js and sws-ui.js, and cross-origin requests are deliberately not intercepted.

scenarios.name: Backup, restore and the sample trap
scenarios.method: Exported a backup, restored a valid one over a populated year, restored an invalid file, and inspected what 'See a sample first' writes.
scenarios.result: Export produces specials-planner-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json wrapping {app,version,exported,state}. Restoring a valid backup replaced a 1,200-cell year with a 1-cell one instantly — no confirm, no undo, no 'this will replace your current year'. Restoring an invalid file alerts and leaves the year intact. 'See a sample first' writes 24 sample cells directly into the real palette2 key with no sample banner and no discard control; the only exit is 'Erase and start over' on the Setup tab.
scenarios.defect: Restore is a one-tap, unconfirmed, irreversible overwrite of the user's whole year, and the sample silently becomes the user's real data.

scenarios.name: Rapid and repeated interaction
scenarios.method: Real dblclick on 'Apply & build my year'; 30 clicks dispatched into the same task; 30 clicks on the welcome primary; ten consecutive week-next clicks on a full year.
scenarios.result: Real double-click: 0 errors, ends on the week grid. 30 synchronous clicks in one task: 29 uncaught 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading value)' because applySetup re-renders and then reads #f-start again — not reachable by a human, but the handler has no re-entrancy guard. 30 clicks on the welcome primary: 448ms, no duplicate state. Ten week jumps on a 1,200-cell year: 74ms, no errors.
scenarios.defect: No user-reachable defect. applySetup reading its own inputs after render() has destroyed them is a latent re-entrancy hazard worth a guard, nothing more.

The research calls this the app's whole reason to exist ('We store lessons against CYCLE POSITION, not calendar dates… This is the single most important feature in the app') and the special-day modal already promises it in words. Store plans as letter+period with a date-keyed override map for one-offs, render the calendar as a projection, and add 'No school today — push everything forward' with an SWS.undo toast.

fixes.title: Fix the lunch-column precedence bug and normalise cells/notes/special shapes
fixes.rationale: `c.lunchAfter=Math.max(0,Math.min(c.periods,+c.lunchAfter??2))` binds unary plus tighter than ??, so a non-numeric lunchAfter yields NaN, which survives both clamps: verified, a state with lunchAfter:'noon' renders 8 columns with zero lunch headers and no error. Separately migrate() accepts cells:[] unchanged (`s.cells=s.cells||{}`), and an array serialises through JSON.stringify as '[]' — every lesson discarded on the next write. Neither is likely from the app's own UI, but both arrive through a hand-edited or legacy backup, which is the one file a teacher hand-carries between devices.

fixes.title: Make the CSV safe to open in Excel
fixes.rationale: The export is otherwise excellent — 201 rows, correct quoting, special-day labels in the Rotation column, 51ms — but the blob carries no UTF-8 BOM (charCodeAt(0) = 68), so 'Señor Nguyễn · 音楽' mojibakes in Excel on Windows, and a cell beginning '=' is written verbatim as a live formula ('=HYPERLINK("http://evil.test",…)' round-tripped intact). The research treats the spreadsheet as the real competitor and this export as the honest escape hatch from it. Prefix the blob with \uFEFF and prefix any cell starting =, +, - or @ with a single quote or a leading tab.

fixes.title: Cap a rotation letter's length and announce the save
fixes.rationale: A 300-character rotation letter is accepted whole and renders a 4,063px-wide chip inside a 118px Day cell, destroying the column (page overflow stays 0 only because .grid-scroll clips it). Slice letters to a handful of characters on entry, the way the app already slices the list to six. Separately the 'Saved' pill is aria-hidden="true" while the live region happily announces week changes and copy counts — the one status a screen-reader user needs from a local-first planner is the one deliberately withheld.

audit.purpose: A local-first lesson planner for specials teachers — art, music, PE, library. You describe your school year once in Setup (first day, last day, which weekdays you teach, how many periods, where lunch falls, your rotation letters, your name) and the app generates every week of the year as a Day x Period grid of contenteditable boxes. A gear on each day marks it a no-class day, which shows a banner and skips the rotation letter so the cycle stays true across breaks. A focused box raises a fixed bottom bar offering 'Fill whole day' and 'Fill all X-days'. Everything lives in one localStorage key ('palette2'); there is no account and no upload. Output paths are the browser's own print (a landscape week grid with a title carrying the teacher's name), a CSV for Sheets/Excel, and a one-file JSON backup with restore. An optional Google Drive save/load block exists but is dead code — CLIENT_ID is empty, so nothing third-party is ever loaded.
audit.structure: One file. No router, no modules, no build step — 2,013 lines of index.html containing the generated studio base (17-1250), a 156-line app layer (1252-1407), the markup (1412-1444) and a single inline classic <script> (1446-2011). <head> loads sws-prefs.js and sws-ui.js as blocking classic scripts (1409-1410); sws-prefs.js finds no .tipbtn and no header.app here and falls through its SPOTS list to 'header .head-row', appending #swsPrefsBtn after the 'Saved' pill. Body is: <header> (1414-1428, position:sticky, --veil background) holding .wrap > .head-row > .logo (a CSS-drawn .mark, h1 'Specials Planner', .tag 'art · music · PE · library') + span.saved#saved[aria-hidden=true], then nav.tabs[aria-label=Views] with two <button class=tab data-view> ('This week', 'Setup'); <main class="wrap" id="view"> (1430), EMPTY in source and written entirely by JS via innerHTML; <div id="live" class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"> (1431); <div id="bar" aria-hidden="true"> (1433-1440), the fixed bottom copy bar holding #bar-hint[aria-live=polite], #bar-day, #bar-letter and #bar-close; and <div id="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="modal-title"> (1442-1444) with an empty .sheet#modal-sheet. There is NO skip link, NO <noscript>, no footer element (the colophon is written into #view as a .footnote div per view), and no .tipbtn — the tip link lives in the Setup tab's footnote text only. State: a single object S = {config, cells, notes, special}; cells keyed 'YYYY-MM-DD|period', notes keyed 'YYYY-MM-DD', special keyed 'YYYY-MM-DD' → label. YEAR is a derived array of {monday, days:[{iso,dow,letter,special}]} rebuilt by buildYear() behind a yearStale flag.

audit.dynamicMarkup: #view is empty in source; render() (1575) hides or shows nav.tabs, syncs aria-current on the two tab buttons, and dispatches to one of three writers, each of which sets view.innerHTML wholesale. renderWelcome() (1585) writes an inline-styled centred hero — a 30px h2 'Plan your whole year once.', a 440px paragraph, and three stacked buttons (#w-fresh 'Start fresh →', #w-sample 'See a sample first', #w-import 'Restore from a backup file') — plus a .footnote. renderWeek() (1622) first calls buildYearIfStale(), then either the 'No weeks yet' card or: a .weeknav.no-print (‹ / › with aria-labels and disabled at the ends, a #wk-jump select carrying one option per week labelled 'Wk n · Aug 24–28, 2026', a Today button, a spacer, a Print button), a .print-title, and .grid-scroll > table.week[aria-label]. The header row is built by string concatenation with a 🍎 th[aria-label=Lunch] inserted after lunchAfter periods and a Notes column last. Each body row carries a .day-gear button (aria-label 'Day settings for Monday Aug 24'), the day name and date, a .chip with the rotation letter coloured by its index modulo 6, an optional .sp-banner, one <div class=box contenteditable role=textbox aria-multiline=true> per period with a full accessible name and data-iso/data-p/data-letter, a td.lunch, and a Notes box. Cell text is then written with textContent in a second pass (1676-1683) — never innerHTML — and four listeners are attached per box (input, focus, paste, keydown). announce() feeds #live with 'Week 3 of 40: Sep 7–11, 2026' on every render. renderSetup() (1805) writes three .card panels — 'Your schedule' (date inputs, the seven .dp day toggles inside a role=group with aria-labelledby, a number input for periods that rebuilds the lunch <select> on change, a rotation-letters text input, a teacher-name input, and 'Apply & build my year'), 'Your data' (Download backup, Restore backup, Export CSV, and an empty #drive-slot that mountDrive() leaves untouched while CLIENT_ID is empty), and 'Start over' — plus a footnote carrying the Stripe tip link. openSpecial(iso) (1759) writes the modal sheet: an h3#modal-title with the date, a paragraph explaining the cycle behaviour, three preset buttons, a #sp-custom input, Save, an optional 'Back to a normal day', and Cancel; it records document.activeElement, focuses the first control, and closeModal() restores focus. onBoxFocus() (1715) raises #bar and rewrites #bar-hint and the letter button's label; hideBar() drops it. Persistence is a 400ms debounce (queueSave) plus an immediate persist() after any structural change, with no pagehide flush.

comfortDefects.issue: Every type size on the primary surface is a hardcoded px and does not respond to the text-size setting. Verified at data-text="xxl": root 16px → 24px while .box stays 13.5px, th 11.5px, .day-name 14px, .day-date 12px, td.lunch span 10.5px, .sp-banner 11.5px.
comfortDefects.fix: Move every one to var(--t-*). The design system's rule 3 is 'Body text never below 16px' — .box is the body text of this app.

comfortDefects.issue: table.week has a hardcoded min-width:840px, so the grid does not scale with --ui-scale either: 460px stays hidden at 414px at every text setting.
comfortDefects.fix: Express as rem (e.g. min-width:52rem) so it grows with the root, and add a narrow-width layout.

comfortDefects.issue: .grid-scroll is background:#fff, a hardcoded literal. In dark mode the whole content surface is white under near-white ink — lesson text measures 1.2:1.

Four more light-only literals survive the theme: .weeknav select #fff (1.2:1 against --ink in dark), .box:focus #FFFDF7, #modal input #fff (white text on white while typing a day label), .saved #55704F.
comfortDefects.fix: var(--field) for inputs and selects, var(--surface-2) for the focus wash, var(--pos) for the saved pill.

comfortDefects.issue: --lunch #EFE6D2 and --block #E9E2D2 are app-local literals with no dark values, so the lunch column and the no-class banner stay cream in dark mode at 1.86:1 and 1.79:1.
comfortDefects.fix: Define both in the dark blocks, or derive them from --surface-2 / --warn-soft.

comfortDefects.issue: The rotation chip sets only a background and inherits color:var(--ink) from the base, giving 2.81–2.95:1 at 13px in light mode, unchanged by contrast:more. The comment above the rule still claims the removed white ink is present.
comfortDefects.fix: Add color:#fff (or --accent-ink) to the .l* variants and delete the stale comment once verified.

comfortDefects.issue: .day-gear is 25x27px and does not grow with --ui-scale — still 27px at Largest text. It is the only route to the app's headline feature.
comfortDefects.fix: min-height/min-width:var(--tap), and stop floating it into the corner of an editable cell.

comfortDefects.issue: .tab is 38px and .dp is 44x38px, both under the 44px --tap floor. .tab reaches 49px at Largest text; .dp does not (fixed height).
comfortDefects.fix: min-height:var(--tap) on both; drop the fixed .dp height.

comfortDefects.issue: #bar is a 101px fixed panel that animates into the thumb zone over the primary surface on every box focus, covering 2 of 5 day rows at 414x720 — against an explicit non-negotiable in the design system.
comfortDefects.fix: Dock the two actions inline beside the focused cell, or pin the bar under the header on narrow viewports.

comfortDefects.issue: Inline styles written from JS bypass the comfort settings entirely: the welcome hero's 30px h2, its 15px paragraph, three buttons with padding:15px and font-size:13px, and a text-transform override inside the teacher-name label.
comfortDefects.fix: Promote each to a class in the app layer using tokens.

comfortDefects.issue: The setup form's label is 12px uppercase and #modal .sub is 13px — both below the 15px instructional floor, and neither scales.
.logo .tag is display:none under 640px, so the one line explaining what the app is for disappears on exactly the device where a new user is most likely to meet it.
comfortDefects.fix: Keep it; wrap the header instead.

comfortDefects.issue: The base's .trust stamp is unused and the privacy promise is grey .footnote prose, which the design system explicitly says users do not believe.
comfortDefects.fix: Put a .trust stamp on the welcome hero — 'no account, nothing uploaded, no student names' is the strongest claim this app has.

comfortDefects.issue: The base's .empty component is unused; the only empty state ('No weeks yet') is a .card with an h2, and an unfilled lesson box shows a bare em dash in --line-2.
The tip jar is not in the header as a .tipbtn pill; it is a sentence inside the Setup tab's footnote, so it is invisible from the week view where the work happens.
comfortDefects.fix: Add the standard header pill; the system's shape for it already exists.

comfortDefects.issue: .tab:not(.active):hover is the only affordance distinguishing the inactive tab from plain text — hover does not exist on the phone this app is meant for.
comfortDefects.fix: Give the inactive tab a persistent border or surface.

navigationDefects.issue: The current view and the current week are not in the URL. There is no hash routing at all — reload always lands on 'This week' at whichever week contains today, and no state is linkable, bookmarkable or reachable by Back.
navigationDefects.fix: Encode view and week in the hash (#/week/12, #/setup).

navigationDefects.issue: Back does nothing inside the app, and nothing is undoable. SWS.undo is loaded via sws-ui.js and called zero times; the only guard anywhere is a confirm() on 'Erase and start over'.
navigationDefects.fix: Wrap doCopy, setSpecial, applyImportedText and resetAll in SWS.undo.

navigationDefects.issue: The Day column is not sticky, so scrolling the 840px grid right to Periods 5-6 or Notes removes the row labels from view entirely (verified at scrollLeft 460 on a 414px viewport).
navigationDefects.fix: position:sticky;left:0 with a z-index and a right-edge shadow on th.day-h and the first td.

navigationDefects.issue: There is no scroll affordance on .grid-scroll — no fade, no arrow, no peeking partial column — so on a phone the app looks like it has three columns.
navigationDefects.fix: A gradient mask on the scroller, or a visible 'swipe for periods 4-6' hint.

navigationDefects.issue: There is no way to see or select a class. Columns are 'Period 1'…'Period n' with no section identity, so the app cannot answer 'who is walking in and where did we leave off with them'.
navigationDefects.fix: A per-slot class label in Setup, surfaced in the column header and the box's accessible name.

navigationDefects.issue: 'Fill all X-days' is scoped to the current week only while its label promises the year — 11 boxes across 2 days measured, against 33-34 matching days in a real year.
navigationDefects.fix: Either widen the scope to YEAR or rename to 'Fill this week's X-days'.

navigationDefects.issue: Restoring a backup replaces the entire year with no confirm, no preview and no undo.
navigationDefects.fix: Describe the file's contents and require a confirm, and keep the previous state for one undo.

navigationDefects.issue: 'See a sample first' writes 24 sample cells into the real store with no banner and no discard path except 'Erase and start over' two clicks away on another tab.
navigationDefects.fix: A dismissible 'You're looking at a sample' bar with 'Clear it and start fresh'.

navigationDefects.issue: The 'No weeks yet' message blames the dates when the actual cause may be workDays; end-before-start, junk dates and non-numeric workDays all produce the same text.

Crossing one week by keyboard costs about 33 Tab stops (35 contenteditable boxes plus five gears) and there is no arrow-key navigation between cells, which is the one convention every user of a grid expects.
navigationDefects.where: index.html:1653-1658 (the box grid), 1707-1710 (onBoxKey handles only Escape and Ctrl+Enter)
navigationDefects.fix: Arrow-key movement between boxes, and Home/End for the row.

navigationDefects.issue: No skip link, despite the base shipping .skip styling, and the header carries the two tabs plus the comfort button before the content on every render.
navigationDefects.fix: Add Skip to content as the first child of body.

navigationDefects.issue: Export paths are split across tabs with no cross-reference: Print sits in the week nav, while CSV and JSON backup live only under Setup.
navigationDefects.fix: Group them, or surface a single 'Share / print this week' affordance from the week view.

navigationDefects.issue: A multi-year span silently stops at 80 weeks with no message, and config.yearEnd keeps the value the user typed, so Setup and the grid disagree.
navigationDefects.fix: Bound by the end date, and say so if a span is refused.

a11yDefects.issue: axe reports 46 color-contrast failures in dark mode (0 in light): lesson text and the week selector at 1.2:1, the day date at 2.31:1, the lunch label at 1.86:1, the special-day banner at 1.79:1, the tab at 2.29:1.
a11yDefects.fix: Replace the six hardcoded light literals with tokens; see comfortDefects.

a11yDefects.issue: The rotation chip is 2.81:1 in light mode at 13px, unaffected by prefers-contrast or the High-contrast setting. axe misses it because the chip's own fill resolves and the text is 600-weight, so it never trips the rule set that runs.
a11yDefects.fix: Set the chip's colour explicitly and re-verify all six.

a11yDefects.issue: The 'Saved' status is aria-hidden="true", so the one confirmation a screen-reader user needs from a local-first app is deliberately withheld — while #live announces week changes and copy counts.
a11yDefects.fix: Announce 'Saved' through #live (throttled), or make the pill a role=status with a timestamp.

a11yDefects.issue: A failed write produces no message of any kind — no alert, no toast, no live-region text — while the visual pill still says Saved.
a11yDefects.fix: Surface a persistent, actionable warning and offer 'Download a backup now'.

a11yDefects.issue: .day-gear is 25x27px against a 44px floor and does not scale with --ui-scale. WCAG 2.5.8 / the system's own rule 4.
.tab (38px) and .dp (44x38px) are also under the floor, and .dp's height is fixed so it never grows.
.box sets outline:none and replaces it with an inset box-shadow in --terra, an app-local literal rather than --focus, so the focus ring does not follow the theme or the high-contrast setting.
a11yDefects.fix: Use var(--focus) and the base focus treatment.

a11yDefects.issue: The modal is a hand-rolled div, not <dialog>: the page behind it is not inert (body overflow stays visible, and the 35 contenteditable boxes remain editable and reachable by a virtual cursor). The Tab trap is JS-only and does not stop a screen reader browsing out of the dialog.
a11yDefects.fix: Use <dialog>.showModal(), which gives inertness, the top layer and Escape for free — the pattern #swsPrefs already uses in the same page.

a11yDefects.issue: #modal keeps role=dialog, aria-modal=true and aria-labelledby="modal-title" in the DOM permanently, including while it is display:none and #modal-title does not exist.
a11yDefects.fix: Set the attributes when opening, or move to <dialog>.

a11yDefects.issue: #bar is aria-hidden="true" in source and toggled to false on show. The toggle is correct, but while hidden the bar's three buttons rely on visibility:hidden to leave the tab order — a CSS property, doing an accessibility job.
a11yDefects.fix: Also toggle inert or hidden on #bar so the two are never out of step.

a11yDefects.issue: #bar-hint is aria-live="polite" and rewrites on every box focus, so tabbing across a row announces 'Monday · Period 1 — Ctrl+Enter for these buttons', then Period 2, then Period 3 — a second announcement layered on top of the box's own accessible name.
a11yDefects.fix: Drop the live region from the hint; the box's name already carries the context.

a11yDefects.issue: Rotation letters are conveyed as a coloured chip plus a single glyph with no text alternative — the box's accessible name says 'Monday Aug 24, period 3' and never mentions which rotation day it is.
a11yDefects.fix: Include the letter in the box's aria-label, and give the chip an accessible name ('rotation day A').

a11yDefects.issue: The header contains an <h1> and each Setup card an <h2>, but the week view has no heading at all — the grid's only label is table[aria-label], so there is no landmark heading to jump to.
a11yDefects.fix: An h2 carrying the week label above the grid.

a11yDefects.issue: No skip link exists, and the base ships the styling for one.
a11yDefects.fix: Add it as the first child of body.

a11yDefects.issue: The 🍎 emoji is the lunch column header with aria-label="Lunch" on the th — correct — but the body cells repeat a vertical-rl 'lunch' string in every row, which a screen reader reads once per day.

audit.printSupport: One paper path, the browser's own, and it is unusually well made for this portfolio — and still not good enough for the ritual it serves. What works, verified under print emulation and by generating real PDFs: @page goes landscape at 9mm; header, .weeknav, #bar, .footnote, .day-gear and #swsPrefsBtn are all display:none; body loses its radial-gradient texture; a .print-title appears carrying 'Specials Planner · Week of Aug 24–28, 2026 · Ms. Rivera'; table.week drops its 840px floor; thead is a table-header-group so column headers repeat; tr gets break-inside:avoid; .box shrinks to 11px with a 52px min-height and its em-dash placeholder is suppressed; and the base's print block neutralises shadows and forces black ink. Nothing about tapping, no navigation chrome and no live regions reach the paper. What fails: with realistic lesson text the table is 1,044px against roughly 748px of usable page, so one 6-period week is 3 pages with only Monday and Tuesday on page one and about 130px of dead space beneath them; at the app's maximum of 10 periods it is 13 columns, 1,909px and 5 pages with a narrowest cell of 44px. At 11px in a ~66px column the text breaks mid-word ('Sketchboo / k covers') because table-layout:fixed gives every period an equal share while Notes keeps 150px and Day keeps 118px. Every rotation letter prints as an identical outlined circle, because the base's ink-saving rule `.chip{background:transparent !important; border:1px solid #999 !important}` (index.html:1219-1224) outranks the app's unimportant `.chip.l0{background:#A8482B}` — the letter survives, the colour coding does not. There is no compact/full toggle, no letter/legal choice, no PDF button, and no print entry point from the Setup tab.
riskyToRestyle: table.week's min-width:840px together with table-layout:fixed and the three fixed column widths (118/44/150px) is what keeps the grid from collapsing into unreadable slivers. Making the width fluid without also giving the period columns a min-width will produce 30px columns on a phone rather than a scroller.

.box is contenteditable, so any change to its padding, min-height or line-height moves the caret and the click target for the app's only input surface. white-space:pre-wrap is load-bearing: the stored format uses real \n characters and nothing else renders them.

outline:none on .box (index.html:1344) is replaced by the inset box-shadow at :1346. Removing either one without the other leaves the app's primary control with no visible focus at all — the design system's rule 5.

.chip is the base's pill component, repurposed here for rotation letters only. Restyling .chip in studio.css changes the rotation letters in this app, and the print rule that blanks .chip fills already does exactly that on paper.

#bar's translateY(110%) + visibility:hidden pair is what keeps its three buttons out of the tab order while hidden; switching to opacity or display alone changes focus behaviour, and the buttons key off currentColor because the bar inverts the page.

The nine app-local tokens at index.html:1264-1276 (--terra, --lunch, --block and friends) are the app's real colour source and have no dark-mode counterparts. Mapping them onto the studio palette is the right move but touches the rotation chips, the lunch column, the no-class banner, the focus ring and the logo mark simultaneously.

header is styled as a bare element selector with position:sticky and z-index 40, and sws-prefs.js resolves its mount point through 'header .head-row'. Renaming or restructuring the header row moves the comfort button somewhere unintended in this app only.

#modal is a hand-rolled overlay with its own scrim, focus trap and keydown handler; #swsPrefs in the same page is a real <dialog>. Converting #modal to <dialog> is the right fix but means deleting the trap at index.html:1793-1802, not layering on top of it.

The entire view is written with innerHTML from three functions, so any CSS transition on a child of #view fires on every render, and :focus-within or :target styling is destroyed each time. Cell text is deliberately written afterwards with textContent — that second pass is the app's only XSS defence for lesson content and must not be folded back into the template.

renderWeek() rebuilds the whole table on every week change, which is why it is fast (74ms for ten jumps on a 1,200-cell year) and also why focus lands wherever refocus() puts it. Introducing per-cell updates would need a focus-preservation strategy the app currently gets for free.
@media print here sets @page{size:landscape} for the whole document; adding a second @page rule elsewhere in the app layer will silently conflict.

The Google Drive block (index.html:1929-1993) injects accounts.google.com/gsi/client at runtime the moment CLIENT_ID is non-empty. It is dead today and sw.js deliberately declines to intercept cross-origin requests, but enabling it would put a third-party script into an app whose entire pitch is that nothing leaves the device.
